title: Both schools: Spirit-wrought faith is idle or love-working
source_text: XLII. Porro ex iis quae tum hisce Thesibus, tum praecedentibus fuerunt exposita, circa naturam fidei salvificae & justificantis, ejusque distinctionem a fide mortua sive otiosa, patet Theologos utriusque Scholae, tum Romanae tum Reformatae, in eo consentire, quod fides illa divina, quae ad Spiritum Sanctum ut authorem referenda est, vel est otiosa & bonis operibus destituta, vel actuosa, & per dilectionem operans.
pass_a_gloss: Furthermore from what has been set out in these theses and the preceding ones concerning the nature of saving and justifying faith and its distinction from dead or idle faith, it is clear that the theologians of both schools, Roman and Reformed, agree in this: that that divine faith which is to be referred to the Holy Spirit as author is either idle and destitute of good works, or active and working through love.
pass_b_english: From this slice and what precedes, both Roman and Reformed schools agree Spirit-authored divine faith is either idle without good works or active working through love.

lemmas.gloss: idle and destitute of good works

choices.why: Shared Galatians phrasing for living faith across schools.
